description: REQ-403's live wallet mutual non-interference audit (a self-described money-safety check) is specified to invoke resolve-identity.mjs's resolveEvmPrivateKey/resolveSolanaSecret 'once per CO-LOCATED running instance with that instance's OWN HOME/ANICCA_HOME (read from REQ-105's registry's homeDir field)'. REQ-105's own seed data sets BOTH of today's two real citizens' homeDir to the literal, identical, bare $HOME value '/Users/anicca', and REQ-105 explicitly asserts this identical value is 'expected, not a bug' because both citizens are co-located. A fresh read of the real resolve-identity.mjs and its own test suite proves this is factually incompatible with how these resolvers actually work: automaton's real ANICCA_HOME is '$HOME/.anicca' (confirmed by install.sh:26, `ANICCA_HOME="${ANICCA_HOME:-$HOME/.anicca}"`, and by resolve-identity.test.mjs's own test 'EVM ③: default-home owner (ANICCA_HOME === $HOME/.anicca) falls back to legacy $HOME/.automaton/wallet.json'), and Franklin's real ANICCA_HOME-equivalent is '$HOME/.blockrun' (confirmed by resolve-identity.test.mjs's own test 'Solana ③: Franklin home (ANICCA_HOME === $HOME/.blockrun) falls back to legacy .solana-session'). The SAME test suite explicitly proves the negative case that matters here: 'EVM ③ gated: foreign spawn (ANICCA_HOME !== $HOME/.anicca, no own wallet yet) does NOT inherit legacy -> null' and the symmetric Solana test -- i.e. resolve-identity.mjs is DELIBERATELY designed to return null for any HOME/ANICCA_HOME value that is not EXACTLY each citizen's own real, distinct root. Passing the bare, shared '/Users/anicca' value that REQ-105 stores for BOTH citizens into resolveEvmPrivateKey({home:'/Users/anicca'})/resolveSolanaSecret({home:'/Users/anicca'}) (whether via the `home` param or an equivalent env.HOME/env.ANICCA_HOME channel -- both were traced and produce the identical outcome) will therefore resolve to null for BOTH citizens, since neither citizen's real root equals the bare $HOME value -- NOT their real signing keys. REQ-403's audit as literally specified would consequently either (a) trivially report 'no collision' between two null results without ever having read either citizen's real key material -- a false sense of security for a requirement whose own text calls this a fail-closed 'security-incident response' gate -- or (b) if a future implementer special-cases null!=null as 'pass', the audit still never proves genuine pairwise inequality of REAL keys, defeating REQ-403's stated purpose entirely. This gap survived two prior review rounds that touched this exact field (FIND-202 added homeDir to REQ-105; FIND-303 scoped REQ-403's live check to co-located instances) without either round checking the field's LITERAL SEED VALUE against resolve-identity.mjs's real, already-tested resolution semantics. It also means REQ-105's own field definition is internally inconsistent: it defines homeDir as 'the citizen's own resolved absolute HOME/ANICCA_HOME directory' (implying each citizen's real, distinct value) while its seed data and 'expected, not a bug' framing store a SHARED, non-distinct, bare-$HOME value that is neither citizen's real ANICCA_HOME.
